texts: pirelli scorpion as plus 3 5000 mile review before i purchased my ariya i did tons of research and concluded that the stock dunlop tires that come on our cars are ass especially living in a somewhat snowy environment i did a lot of research on new tires so i wanted to share my thoughts and decision process in case anyone else is in the market i also considered the michelin crossclimate 2 and the continental crosscontact lx25 but ultimately chose the pirellis based on a tire rack test our cars are extremely quiet and honestly feel like they should be wearing an infiniti badge so road noise and ride comfort were major factors for me between the tire rack results and widespread feedback online the reported range loss and increased road noise ruled out the crossclimates if you live in an area with severe snow they are a solid option but in my opinion they are overkill for most midwest states my 5000 mile review i inflate these tires to the eu spec 38 psi im not a tire testing expert just a regular joe giving my thoughts a lot of my thoughts will align with tireracks test i purchased my car with 4700 miles and changed out the stock dunlops at 5400 miles range a no change from the oem dunlops i get 280290 miles in the summer hand calculated not gom and so far ive been getting about 191210 miles in the winter comfortroad noise a the difference is night and day the pirellis suit the car perfectly and complement the luxury ride these cars should have the dunlops felt like concrete sending harsh reverberations into the cabin over potholes and bridge expansion joints that is no longer an issue even after 5000 miles these are easily the quietest tires i have ever owned rain a great hydroplaning resistance and overall wet traction compared to the oem dunlops ive had very few traction issues with the capabilities of the car dry a excellent grip around corners the steering while lighter than the dunlops i think offers much more road feedback and you can tell what the car is doinggoing to do ive had to emergency stops several times almost blasting rogue deer and it brought the behemoth to a stop with no drama snow b i am very happy with the snow grip these provide and would say they are quite possibly the best allseason tires i have owned i do not believe they are even 3peakmountainsnowflake rated we recently received about six inches of snow in the midwest and i felt confident everywhere i drove they perform well on unplowed plowed and slushy roads i have intentionally stopped on steep hills and accelerated normally in snow mode without any wheel spin ice can still be a bit sketchy though these cars are heavy so they can slide longer during abrupt stops plan accordingly give yourself extra stopping distance and you will be fine wear no changes or abnormal wear at 38 psi i plan to provide updates as the tires age i liked them so much that i also put them on my wifes honda crv hybrid and the impressions are the same as above there was no change in fuel economy grip improved significantly and the ride quality went from feeling like a honda to feeling like an acura the difference really is that noticeable

poor global air quality from co2 emissions should be a major concern for humans and the habitability of this planet that it is not is a clear sign of our future biases of all issues that receive wide public discourse today climate change from co2 emissions summons the most attempts at realistic futuristic thinking what will happen to the climate and what will that do to the earth those are questions whose answers inherently require predictions and thoughtful thought about the future sometimes those predictions even range beyond the end of the 21st century a rarity in any context with climate change alarmism about catastrophic climactic events steals the show dialogue centers on debate about the wide range of potential impacts that co2 emissions may have on the the planets climate and the secondary effects thereof but at the root of it all there is a central fact that is not debatable humans have been emitting co2 into the open atmosphere at great and everincreasing rates since the start of the industrial revolution this is not debatable because we can directly measure it we can see that the presence of co2 in the atmosphere climbs every year currently by two to three parts per million ppm and now sits at a concentration of around 425 ppm source climategov and lest you think humans might not be causing that increase or at least the vast majority of it we know from chemistry that the combustion of hydrocarbons results in a certain quantity of co2 released through straightforward mass balance calculations we can prove that our rate of global consumption of oil natural gas and coal which are also measured quantities corresponds to the observed increase in atmospheric co2 climate change is one impact of these increasing co2 levels its the only one that gets talked about but thats not to say its the only one that exists poor global air quality from unhealthy concentrations of co2 may be just as dire and immediate a concern for humans we should probably talk about that too that we dont i believe is strong evidence of our future biases at work sleepy humans if you ever fell asleep in a college lecture dont be too hard on yourself or on the lecturer it may not have been entirely due to your drinking the night before or the dullness of the professor lecture halls are enclosed spaces with lots of humans exhaling co2 even with ventilation they can often achieve co2 levels well in excess of 1000 ppm that happens to be the level at which humans start to feel the ill effects of high co2 concentrations which include drowsiness and discomfort today the global average atmospheric co2 concentration is far below that threshold 425 ppm and growing at only 2 to 3 ppm per annum that doesnt sound like a lot not even an extra 1 added each year doesnt seem like something we need to worry about at all but lets put our realistic futurism hats on and allow the future thinking parts of our brain to wander where few ever go without some fantasy involved more than a few decades in the future lets go a few centuries if we continue to release co2 into the atmosphere at a rate of 2 to 3 ppm per year it will only take 200 to 300 years to add another 600 parts per million and exceed that 1000 ppm threshold whats going to happen then when the whole world is a sleepy lecture hall unless we all plan on buying bottled air from aloysius ohare the enterprising tycoon from dr seusss the lorax at some point the population at large may have to deal with a health crisis induced by chronic overexposure to co2 it stands to reason that other species may be similarly affected why do we not talk about this risk who cares about climate change if well all be sleeping and yawning our way through life potentially with a myriad of other chronic health problems from co2 concentrations we arent evolutionarily designed to accommodate im being facetious only a little here this issue seems important hell it seems like it might help the case for policies that support reductions in emissions so why doesnt at least a little bit of our discourse focus on the potential health risks of poor air quality from rising co2 levels i think there are two reasons two biases in our future thinking that prevent this issue from taking root 1 we struggle with conceptualizing time periods even only slightly longer than our own life climate change is a multicentury process despite its slow incrementalism we manage to make it real for the public through alarmism we focus on climactic tipping point dates and points of no return all things expected to occur in the next 10 years thats the immediate future something that will affect our own lives soon its graspable the march toward truly poor global air quality on the other hand is 200 or 300 years away sometime in the early middle future the steadiness of this march may be unnerving but the steadiness at an apparently low rate prevents us from grasping a tipping point in the immediate future thus the problem remains 200 to 300 years away firmly beyond our own lives and the ken of our typical conceptualizations of the future 200 years though is a woefully short amount of time even on the scale recorded human history some of us will have grandchildren alive then if i were to sire a child at the age of 83 and that child sired a child at 80 and that child lived to 80 that could be me 2 technology will save the day 200 years is way more than long enough to allow our usual science fictional imaginings to take over ive written previously about how humans have come to think of technology as the cavalry coming to save us given enough time and 200 years would be plenty of time in popular imaginings technology will find a way to save the day in the case of emissions certainly well find an alternative to fossil fuels or well find a way to strip co2 out of the atmosphere so the thinking goes its a very real real risk based on what ive observed and studied i dont share that thinking im not that optimistic that 200 years is enough time to cut enough emissions nor am i optimistic about technology to find an economic solution to strip co2 from the air fossil fuel consumption will probably be steady or even growing for many decades to come and consumption will require many more decades to trail off look below at this projection from exxons global outlook report this predicts oil and gas consumption will rise globally through at least 2050 with only coal showing a meaningful decline replaced to a large extent by cheap natural gas with this consumption co2 emissions will continue apace through this time frame and well beyond primary energy quadrillion btu source exxon global outlook report what is more even if we find viable alternative energy sources my bet is on nuclear energy it will take decades to maybe centuries to replace the energy infrastructure we already have in order to take advantage of it as such even going gangbusters with nuclear wind and solar it may take all of 200 years or more to materially reduce co2 emissions in a base case scenario we may just barely make it before concentrations reach 1000 ppm on the technology side im outright pessimistic about co2 capture and sequestration technologies actively removing co2 is generally very expensive and challenging it may even be a fools errand when it comes to stripping it out of the open atmosphere akin to spitting in the ocean to cause sealevel rise well save this discussion for another time but suffice it to say an educated study of this issue would arrive at the same conclusion a good case study in realistic futurism this post and for that matter this reddit community is not directly concerned with climate change or co2 emissions its concerned with instilling a sense of realistic futurism that our discourse and mindsets so often lack realistic futurism is nothing more than a common sense approach to the future a big part of it is forcing ourselves to overcome our preference for fantastical technological thinking another big part is forcing ourselves to think into the future on timescales slightly longer than a few decades when you combine the two important issues emerge that are not receiving attention today but should be this is one of those issues we have a major risk of poor global air quality albeit in 200 years and we know well be technologically challenged in meeting it we should start talking about it now along with our other concerns about emissions

2000km harley 1200 roadster ownership update so got a few requests for an ownership update post on my last post here when i had just picked up the 1200 roadster before i do the pros and cons let me give a quick rundown of the changes ive made and the cost these dont include general gear purchases like gloves jackets etc that ive made most of the spend so far has gone into sorting the bike properly and improving rideability not cosmetic mods performance intakeexhaust vance hines short shots used 55000 rinehart heavy breather air filter 24000 comfort utility new seat 10000 leather heat guard 2500 navigation electronics pro play navigation system new 16500 mechanical reliability new original harley battery 9000 previous nonharley battery sparked and almost caused a fire lesson learnt new clutch plates clutch system 31000 old clutch completely gave out fit finish work wiring cleanup under the tank tank raise 2000 you can clearly see the difference compared to my older post the wiring under the tank is much cleaner now and the bike looks far more sorted overall so in total ive put down another 15l over and above ancillary costs fuel insurance registration etc now the pros 1 the power of the bike is fantastic that 1200 evo has crazy torque and can haul ass even above 100kmh not that im driving all that fast 2 ive ridden a few of the bigger harleys in this time and i keep coming back to my roadster for how light it is comparatively 3 the vh short shots completely transform the bike they are super bassy and loud compared to the stock exhaust i just get a bit jittery around cops but im a lawyer so i dont expect too many issues if i do get pulled over they are usually lenient with members of the bar 4 does not stand out at all honestly before i got the vh you could not hear this bike in traffic which was quite nice it was like a subtle bike just rolling up on you i also dont put 5000 add ons and have tried to keep it damn near as clean as possible except the navigation which was a necessity cons 1 heat management is the biggest drawback in slowmoving traffic or summer conditions the aircooled engine throws off a lot of heat especially on the right leg the leather heat guard helps to an extent but it doesnt eliminate the issue this is not a bike youd want to be stuck with in bumpertobumper traffic on a daily basis ive had bad experiences in traffic already where i need to pull over and hop off the bike wont be usable in peak ncr summer 2 the bikes clutch is heavy even with the new clutch my arm starts killing me in bumper traffic thinking of getting a rekluse auto clutch to fix this issue 3 fuel efficiency is another clear downside realworld mileage hovers around 1416 kml in the city and about 1820 kml on the highway which is significantly lower than most middleweight motorcycles running costs especially with rising fuel prices will be steep going ahead 4 parts availability and the ownership ecosystem require patience routine service is manageable but specific parts and performance upgrades are expensive and sometimes take time to source the ownership isnt as stressfree or predictable as i thought it would be 5 had other issues such as paint chipping loose wiring and oiling issues but these were more to do with it being a secondhand purchase and less to do with my time owning the bike per se so not getting into those 6 a uniquely ncrspecific con is the 15year ownership cap this bike was registered in 2016 which means ill hit that limit sooner rather than later while id love to keep this bike longterm the reality is that it probably wont stay with me forever unless i park it in my garage and occasionally take it out under the cover of darkness some concluding thoughts overall the bike has performed exactly to my expectations which ill admit were set at a mediumtolow bar given the reputation and realities of harley ownership in india one pleasant surprise has been the harley community itself its generally quite chill and welcoming im 25 while the average age in most groups is easily 45 so i do feel a bit out of place at times but ive never had a bad experience in fact ive met some genuinely nice people and made good contacts through sunday rides a lot of the pain points of owning this bike are less about the motorcycle itself and more about the ncr climate most of these issues practically disappear in winter riding finally ill be honest i bought this as my first bike purely for emotional reasons with zero practical intent and judged on that metric alone it genuinely feels like one of the best purchases ive made oc post

how does the petrochemical industry contribute to air pollution the petrochemical industry plays a vital role in producing everyday materials like plastics lubricants paints and fertilizers however these benefits come with an environmental cost air pollution petrochemical plants release several harmful gases during production transport and refining processes 1 emissions during manufacturing during the conversion of crude oil and natural gas into petrochemical products various chemical reactions take place these processes emit volatile organic compounds vocs nitrogen oxides nox sulfur dioxide so and particulate matter pm25 these gases contribute to the formation of groundlevel ozone and smog which pollute the air and harm both people and the environment 2 combustion byproducts when petrochemical products such as fuels are burned they emit carbon dioxide co and methane ch major greenhouse gases responsible for climate change in addition incomplete combustion in industrial furnaces and boilers produces carbon monoxide co and fine particulates that degrade air quality further 3 fugitive emissions petrochemical plants often experience small continuous leaks called fugitive emissions from valves pipelines and tanks even in small quantities these leaks release large amounts of vocs into the atmosphere worsening local air quality over time 4 storage and how often should i change my hairstyle while it can be great to give your look an update or boost your confidence with a hairstyle change it ultimately depends on how often you decide to change it there isnt a clear standard for this so focus on achieving an optimal balance among these aspects a typical person changes hisher hairstyle every 6 to 8 weeks this time gap is ideal because your hairs take this time to grow and relax also if you are using any chemical or heated tools on your hair this time is ideal for them to relax and revitalize if you like doing protective styles like braids twists wigs or sewins it is highly advisable to switch styles every 4 to 6 weeks wearing a protective style for too long can cause scalp buildup breakage or thinning of the edges taking a break from your natural hair will promote healthy growth haircuts are always best when updated regularly shorter hairstyles will need to be shaped every 3 to 4 weeks whereas longer hairstyles will take 8 to 12 weeks for a trim before being shaped again colored or chemically treated hair will need to be updated more frequently since frequently processed hair tends to weaken your lifestyle is also important if your occupation climate and lifestyle require easytomanage hair you may choose fewer styles however if fashion values and expression mean much to you then frequent changes are also perfectly acceptable provided that they are taken care of properly when your hair is sending signals like being overly dry breaking off or being irritated on your scalp it is a sign that you need to hold on rather than go for a different look your healthy hair should always be your priority when your hair is in its best condition you will have the freedom to change hairstyles as you deem fit

offering evidence or logic the speaker tries to make you agree by threatening harm punishment or negative consequences if you dont definition an appeal to force attempts to persuade someone to accept a conclusion by appealing to fear power or coercion not logic or evidence example youd better agree that my plan is best if you dont you might lose your job thats not reasoning thats a threat disguised as an argument the problem fear might change someones behavior but it doesnt make an argument valid a true argument should stand on evidence not intimidation in short logic convinces the persons argument to make it easier to attack or dismiss instead of responding to the real argument which might be valid complex or wellreasoned they build a weaker version of it knock that down and act as if theyve defeated the original point a real argument is often valid or strong logically connected welldeveloped subtle and nuanced hard to refute a straw man argument is oversimplified misstated or distorted based on poor assumptions easier to criticize than the real thing example person a we should have some regulations on social media person b oh so you want the government to control everything we say thats a straw man it twists the claim into something extreme and easier to reject in short the straw man doesnt fight the real argument it fights a weaker version that never truly existed logic 101 lesson 6 ad hominem against the person an ad hominem fallacy happens when someone attacks the person making an argument instead of addressing the argument itself arguments are built from claims factual evidence inferences conclusions people on the other hand have character circumstances actions when someone commits an ad hominem they ignore the reasoning and go after the person their motives background or behavior as if that alone disproves the argument example you cant trust her opinion on climate change shes not even a scientist that attacks who she is not what she upper mustang trek a journey into nepals hidden kingdom the upper mustang trek is one of the most unique and culturally rich trekking experiences in nepal located in the rain shadow of the himalayas upper mustang feels very different from other trekking regions the landscape is dry rugged and dramatic with deep valleys colorful rock formations and ancient cave dwellings carved into cliffs at the same time the region preserves centuriesold tibetan culture that remains largely unchanged often referred to as the last forbidden kingdom upper mustang was previously restricted to outsiders until the early 1990s even today special permits are required which helps protect its culture and environment for travelers seeking something beyond classic himalayan treks the upper mustang trek offers a unique blend of history stunning scenery and living traditions why the upper mustang trek is different from other treks one of the main reasons the upper mustang trek stands out is its geography unlike everest or annapurna this region lies north of the main himalayan range and receives very little rainfall as a result the trail is dusty and desertlike with wide open skies and strong winds shaping the land additionally the culture has a distinctly tibetan feel prayer flags mani walls monasteries and whitewashed villages line the trail many locals still practice traditional farming and trade and the pace of life feels slow and grounded due to restricted access the upper mustang trekking route also feels quieter and less crowded this makes the experience more personal and immersive compared to busier routes upper mustang trek route and key highlights the upper mustang trek usually begins after a flight or drive to jomsom from there the trail follows the kali gandaki river northward through villages such as kagbeni chele and ghami each village has its own character with flatroofed houses narrow alleys and ancient monasteries one of the major highlights is lo manthang the walled capital of upper mustang surrounded by mud brick walls this historic town is home to royal palaces important monasteries and vibrant festivals if you visit at the right time exploring lo manthang feels like stepping back in time along the way trekkers also encounter sky caves carved into cliffs long suspension bridges and high mountain passes offering sweeping views of the nilgiri dhaulagiri and annapurna ranges culture and traditions on the upper mustang trek culture is at the heart of the upper mustang trek the people of mustang follow tibetan buddhism and religion plays a significant role in their daily lives monasteries are not just places of worship but also centers of learning and community festivals such as tiji held in lo manthang are vibrant and meaningful events that feature masked dances and rituals intended to ward off evil spirits even outside festival times prayer wheels chortens and chanting monks create a strong spiritual atmosphere because upper mustang trekking takes you through living villages rather than remote camps cultural interaction feels genuine and respectful when approached with care landscape and nature on the upper mustang trek the landscape of the upper mustang trek is striking and unusual instead of green forests you see barren hills deep canyons and layered cliffs shaped by wind and erosion the colors range from red and orange to gray and gold changing throughout the day with the light despite the dry terrain life thrives here you may spot blue sheep eagles and other wildlife adapted to harsh conditions farming fields appear as green patches against the desert background illustrating how people have thrived here for centuries this dramatic environment is one of the main reasons travelers choose the upper mustang trek over more typical himalayan routes best time for the upper mustang trek the best time for the upper mustang trek is from april to october because the region lies in a rain shadow it is one of the few treks in nepal that can be done during the summer monsoon months spring brings mild temperatures and clear views while summer offers warmer days and access when other regions are wet autumn is also popular due to stable weather and festivals winter is possible but challenging as cold temperatures and snow can make high passes difficult permits and preparation for the upper mustang trek the upper mustang trek requires special permits trekkers require a restricted area permit and must travel with a registered trekking agency and a licensed guide this regulation helps preserve culture and supports local communities physical preparation is important but this trek is more about endurance than technical difficulty daily walking hours are moderate and altitude gain is gradual
